Note: Figure not drawn to scale. In right triangle $PQR$ shown, what is the measure of $R$?
explanation: Choice C is correct. The sum of the measures of the interior angles of any triangle is $180^\circ$. In right triangle $PQR$, angle $Q$ is the right angle, so $m\angle Q = 90^\circ$. The diagram shows that $m\angle P = 38^\circ$. Using the triangle angle sum theorem: $m\angle P + m\angle Q + m\angle R = 180^\circ$. Substituting the known values gives $38^\circ + 90^\circ + m\angle R = 180^\circ$. Solving for $m\angle R$: $m\angle R = 180^\circ - 38^\circ - 90^\circ = 52^\circ$. Therefore, the measure of angle $R$ is $52^\circ$.
